question: Assume the JTB definition of Knowledge, which suggests that "Knowledge is a Justified True Belief". If our only available epistemic states are Knowledge and Belief, what are the two problems JTB runs into? Ignore Gettier problems.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The two problems seem to be that any attempt to justify a belief quickly generates an infinite chain of further justifications (since each justifier would itself need to be known rather than merely believed), and that we would then have no non-arbitrary way to decide when a belief counts as sufficiently justified versus merely held. This leaves JTB unable to mark a stable boundary between the two epistemic states without either endless deferral or an unmotivated stopping point.

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The two problems JTB runs into are the problem of the external world and the problem of other minds. Under the constraint that we only have access to knowledge and belief states, JTB cannot bridge the gap from internal justification to confirming that the external world exists as we believe it does (rather than being a persistent illusion), nor can it establish that other people have minds rather than merely behaving as if they do. Both issues persist even after setting aside Gettier cases, because they concern whether the truth and justification conditions can ever be jointly satisfied for these domains without additional epistemic resources.

9.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With truth and justification as two independent dimensions you get four cells. JTB makes only one of them Knowledge and puts everything else under the single umbrella Belief.

Truth x Justification

* Justified True Belief = Knowledge
* Justified False Belief = Belief
* Unjustified True Belief = Belief
* Unjustified False Belief = Belief

Hence the non-Knowledge category Belief is heterogeneous.

1. Justified False Belief. A justified false belief is epistemically good in the justification respect and bad in the truth respect. JTB is forced to call it mere Belief, because it is not true. That lumps a belief that is well supported and for all the subject knows true together with plain unjustified false belief. The epistemic value of justification is therefore invisible once the state is non-knowledge, and Belief becomes a grab-bag of justified and unjustified false beliefs.

2. Unjustified True Belief. An unjustified true belief is epistemically bad in the justification respect and good in the truth respect. JTB is forced to call it mere Belief, because it lacks justification. That lumps a lucky true hit together with a justified false belief and with an unjustified false belief. The epistemic value of truth is therefore invisible once the state is non-knowledge, and Belief again conflates beliefs that differ in a crucial way.

On a Knowledge / Belief only taxonomy the complement of Knowledge within Belief has to contain both JF and UT. You therefore lose any way of distinguishing a belief that is good because it is justified from a belief that is bad because it is unjustified, and a belief that is good because it is true from a belief that is bad because it is false. That is the classic pre-Gettier over-inclusion / under-differentiation of Belief.

3.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With JTB the logical space of belief + truth + justification is

J+T = Knowledge
J+F = justified false belief
UJ+T = unjustified true belief
UJ+F = unjustified false belief

If the only epistemic categories we are allowed to use are Knowledge and Belief, Belief has to do the work of the three non-knowledge cells. JTB therefore forces an
over-lumping of epistemically distinct cases.

* Justified false belief. J+F is not knowledge because it is not true. On a Knowledge/Belief taxonomy it must be called mere Belief. That makes a justified false belief epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief UJ+F, and makes a belief which is epistemically good in the sense of being justified sit in the same
category as a belief which is bad in both respects. In effect justification is lost once truth fails.

* Unjustified true belief. UJ+T is not knowledge because it is not justified. On a Knowledge/Belief taxonomy it must also be called mere Belief. That makes an
unjustified but true belief epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief UJ+F and from a justified false belief J+F. In effect truth is lost once justification fails, and the true-but-lucky case is lumped together with outright false belief.

So the Belief category becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag of J+F, UJ+T and UJ+F. JTB therefore cannot register that a justified false belief is better than an unjustified false belief, nor that a true unjustified belief is different from a false belief. The two cells J+F and UJ+T are the ones JTB has to collapse into Belief, which is why the analysis is coarse-grained even before the Gettier cases.

6.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On a JTB picture Knowledge = justified + true + belief. If Knowledge and Belief are the only two epistemic kinds, then every non-knowledge state is just Belief.

That makes the Belief class massively heterogeneous. In particular JTB with only two kinds cannot make room for the two intermediate epistemic positions that are clearly non-knowledge but are not the same as each other:

* Justification without truth. A justified false belief is justified and is a belief, but it is not true and so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On the Knowledge/Belief dichotomy it has to be classed as mere Belief. Hence justified belief that turns out false is not distinguished from unjustified belief. You lose the distinct, epistemically good state of being justified and still being wrong.

* Truth without justification. An unjustified true belief is true and is a belief, but it is not justified and so by JTB it is not Knowledge. On the Knowledge/Belief dichotomy it has to be classed as mere Belief. Hence a lucky true belief is not distinguished from a false belief. You lose the distinct state of being right by luck / without warrant.

So Belief becomes a trash-heap of justified-false, unjustified-true and unjustified-false states. Knowledge is homogeneous - justified true belief - but Belief has to do the work of three different epistemic situations, justification can obtain without truth and truth can obtain without justification, and the dichotomy cannot register that difference. That is why a richer taxonomy with at least justified belief, unjustified belief, justified true belief, etc. is normally introduced.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On a JTB picture with the state space { Know , Believe } the
three JTB ingredients Justification, Truth and Belief collapse as soon as
you fall out of Knowledge.

If an agent believes p

* Believes p ∧ p true ∧ Justified  → Know p
* Believes p ∧ p true ∧ Unjustified → Believe p
* Believes p ∧ p false ∧ Justified  → Believe p
* Believes p ∧ p false ∧ Unjustified → Believe p

Everything that is not Justified True Belief is just ‘Belief’.  In
particular justification and truth become invisible outside of knowledge.

That gives the classic pre-Gettier loss of discriminability.

* Justified false belief is not knowledge because it is not true, so on the
two-state scheme it is just Believe.  Justification is therefore lost for
false beliefs: a justified false belief and an unjustified false belief are
epistemically indistinguishable, both are mere belief, although intuitively
the former is epistemically better.
* Unjustified true belief is not knowledge because it is not justified, so
on the two-state scheme it is just Believe.  Truth is therefore lost for
unjustified beliefs: an unjustified true belief and a justified false belief
are both mere belief, so JTB makes a lucky true belief epistemically on a
par with a well-justified false belief.

In effect JTB can only mark the conjunction Justified+True+Believe as
Know.  Justification without truth and truth without justification are both
swallowed by the undifferentiated Believe state, so the independent
epistemic value of justification and of truth is erased once you are out of
knowledge.  That is the justified-false-belief problem and the unjustified-
true-belief/lucky-truth problem, the two non-Gettier collapses that a
binary Know/Believe taxonomy forces on JTB.

2.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With JTB the epistemic field is normally True/False x Justified/Unjustified.

Knowledge = T & J & B

If Knowledge and Belief are the only live kinds then

Knowledge = T & J
Belief = not-T&J

i.e. everything that is not a justified true belief is just lumped together as ‘belief’. The 2x2 is then collapsed to one cell.

That collapse erases two distinct epistemic positions that the matrix would otherwise make room for.

1. Justified false belief, JFB.  F & J. It is not knowledge because it is false, but it is epistemically better than an unjustified false belief. On a Knowledge / Belief only taxonomy it has to be classed as mere Belief, so a justified falsehood is treated as epistemically on a par with an unjustified falsehood. Justification therefore disappears as a discriminator once you are out of the knowledge cell.

2. Unjustified true belief, UTUB. T & ~J. It is true and so epistemically better than a false belief, but it is not knowledge because it is unjustified, e.g. a lucky guess. On a Knowledge / Belief only taxonomy it too has to be classed as mere Belief, so a lucky true belief is treated as epistemically on a par with a plain false or with an unjustified false belief. Truth therefore disappears as a discriminator once you are out of the knowledge cell.

In effect ‘Belief’ becomes a heterogeneous catch-all for JFB, UTUB and ~T&~J. You can no longer mark the epistemic difference between a justified falsehood and an unjustified falsehood, nor between a true lucky belief and a false/unjustified belief. That is the non-Gettier cost of having only Knowledge = JTB and Belief as the two available states.

5.text:
With the traditional analysis

K p  iff  B p & T p & J p

J p has to be cashed out in the resources you have. If the only
epistemic categories you allow are B and K there is no independent
category 'justified but not known' to do the work of J.

Hence J p has to be either a belief or a piece of knowledge.

* J as belief.  Justification is then just more belief.  A belief p is
justified iff it is based on a belief q that supports p.  That makes
justification truth independent: q can be false, so you can have a
true p justified by a false q, i.e. a justified false belief can do the
justifying work for a true belief.  In particular J collapses into
B and the analysis becomes

K p  iff  B p & T p & B q 

so in effect K is just T B. The justification clause adds nothing, and
if you insist on the justification of the justifier you get the familiar
foundationalist trilemma: an infinite regress of B's, B1 justifies B2
justifies B3..., a vicious circle B1 -> B2 -> B1, or an arbitrary
dogmatic stopping point of unjustified beliefs.

* J as knowledge.  Justification is then a knowledge that p is so. 
To know p you must know that you have a good reason for p.  That is

K p  iff  B p & T p & K r

for some r that supports p.  Knowledge is then defined in terms of
knowledge.  In the limit you need K that you know that you know...,
i.e. an infinite ascent of higher order knowledge, or else a closed
circle of mutually supporting knowledge claims.  The justification
condition becomes trivially redundant, K p iff K p & T p & B p, and
the analysis is circular rather than reductive.

So on the impoverished ontology {B,K} the J in JTB cannot be made an
independent third condition: it is either redundant and circular if it
is identified with knowledge, or it collapses into further belief and
gives you regress / circularity and the possibility of a true belief
being justified by, and so epistemically dependent on, a false belief.
That is the classic regress-circularity problem for the justification
condition, the reason why a non-circular JTB needs an epistemic
category distinct from mere belief and knowledge, e.g. warrant,
entitlement, safety, etc.

8.text:
Under JTB Knowledge is a species of Belief. Knowledge = Justified & True & Belief, Belief is the
residual class.

If Knowledge and Belief are the only atomic epistemic kinds that you allow, every
attitude you take to a proposition has to be classified as either Knowledge or as
mere Belief. That makes Belief a heterogeneous catch-all.

* Justified false belief. A p which is justified and believed but false is not
Knowledge because Knowledge requires truth. It is not a distinct epistemic kind
under the two-state taxonomy, so it has to be classified as mere Belief. You
therefore lose the ability to mark a false belief that is epistemically creditable,
justified, as different from an unjustified or careless false belief. Justified
false belief has no home, it collapses into the undifferentiated Belief class.

* True but unjustified belief. A p which is true and believed but not justified is
not Knowledge because Knowledge requires justification. It too has to be classified
as mere Belief. You therefore lose the ability to mark a true belief that is
epistemically defective, a lucky true belief, as different from a justified true
belief. Unjustified true belief has no home, it collapses into the same Belief
class as justified false belief, unjustified false belief, etc.

Hence with only Knowledge vs Belief the Belief state becomes the disjunction of
justified false belief, unjustified true belief and unjustified false belief. You
can no longer keep apart epistemic credit for justification from epistemic credit
for truth, and you cannot give a distinct epistemic status to justified false
beliefs and to lucky true beliefs. That is the lack of epistemic granularity that
the JTB account inherits once the taxonomy is restricted to the two states.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: On the JTB picture Knowledge is the subset of Belief which is both true and justified. If Belief is taken as the complement of Knowledge then Belief is a heterogeneous grab-bag.

Knowledge = B & J & T

Belief = not [ B & J & T ] = ¬J & T? & B or ¬T & B etc

So every non-knowledge belief is just ‘belief’. That means the category
Belief has to contain both

* True but unjustified belief, i.e. a true belief that is lucky, and
* Justified but false belief, i.e. a rationally supported error,

and, more generally, false justified belief and false unjustified belief together.

In particular you get no distinct epistemic state for justification
detached from truth and no distinct epistemic state for truth detached
from justification.

1. The justification without truth problem. A justified false belief is
epistemically good in the sense of being responsibly held, responsibly
informed and responsive to the evidence, yet on JTB with only
Knowledge vs Belief it is not knowledge and it is lumped in with mere
mere belief, on a par with an unjustified false belief. You lose the
ability to say that a person can be epistemically responsible even when
wrong. Justification has epistemic value even when it fails to make the
belief true.

2. The truth without justification problem. An unjustified true belief
is true, so it gets the truth value right, yet it is not knowledge and
on the two-state scheme it is lumped in with mere belief, on a par with
a justified false belief. You lose the ability to say that lucky true
belief is epistemically defective. Truth has epistemic value even when
it is not earned by justification.

Hence ‘Belief’ becomes disjunctive: it is the union of
unjustified true beliefs, justified false beliefs and unjustified false
beliefs. One cannot mark off a distinct state of justified non-knowledge
or of true non-knowledge, and the normative differences between
responsible error and lucky truth are erased. That is the familiar
heterogeneity/lack-of-intermediate-state objection to JTB apart from
the Gettier cases.

PRIVATE REFLECTION: The JTB analysis under a binary Know/Believe taxonomy collapses the 2x2 truth × justification space into Know = B & J & T and Belief = ¬[B & J & T].

That forces two non-Gettier losses of discriminability that most colleagues converge on:

* Justification without truth. A justified false belief is not knowledge because it is false, so on Knowledge/Belief it is classed as mere Belief. 2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about JTB under a binary epistemic taxonomy {Knowledge, Belief} and Gettier is to be ignored.

With truth and justification as independent dimensions we have four cells:
* J+T+B = Knowledge
* J+F+B = justified false belief
* UJ+T+B = unjustified true belief
* UJ+F+B = unjustified false belief

On a Knowledge/Belief only taxonomy Knowledge = J+T+B and everything else is forced into the single residual class Belief. Belief therefore becomes heterogeneous.

The dominant view in round 0 is that this collapse erases two independent epistemic discriminations:

1. Justification without truth is lost. A justified false belief is not knowledge because it lacks truth, so it must be called mere Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief. Justification has no distinct non-knowledge status; a responsibly held error is lumped with a careless error. 2. Truth without justification is lost. An unjustified true belief is not knowledge because it lacks justification, so it must be called mere Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth has no distinct non-knowledge status; a lucky true hit is lumped with a well-justified falsehood. In effect truth is invisible once justification fails.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about the coarse-graining forced by a binary Know/Believe taxonomy under JTB = B & T & J.

Truth is therefore invisible once justification fails; you cannot mark that a lucky true belief is epistemically defective relative to knowledge, and a true belief is conflated with false/unjustified belief.

6.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question asks for the two non-Gettier problems JTB faces when the only epistemic kinds allowed are Knowledge and Belief.

Majority consensus in round 0: with JTB Knowledge = Belief ∧ Justified ∧ True, the complement Belief has to contain all non-knowledge cases. Truth and Justification are independent dimensions giving four cells:

J+T = Knowledge
J+F = justified false belief
UJ+T = unjustified true belief
UJ+F = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief the last three cells are forced into the single Belief state, making Belief a heterogeneous grab-bag and erasing independent epistemic value of justification and truth outside knowledge.

Problem 1, justification without truth: justified false belief J+F is not knowledge because false, so must be called mere Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from unjustified false belief UJ+F and from unjustified true belief UJ+T. Intuitively a justified error is epistemically better than an unjustified error, but the two-state taxonomy cannot register that; justification is invisible once truth fails.

Problem 2, truth without justification: unjustified true belief UJ+T is not knowledge because unjustified, so must be called mere Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from justified false belief J+F and from UJ+F. Intuitively a lucky true belief is epistemically defective compared with justified true belief, and also different from a false belief; truth is invisible once justification fails.

Hence Belief = J+F ∨ UJ+T ∨ UJ+F. Knowledge is homogeneous; Belief is disjunctive. The two-state scheme cannot mark a distinct state of justified non-knowledge or true non-knowledge.

Colleague 10 frames the two problems as external world and other minds, i.e., whether justification/truth can ever be jointly satisfied for those domains without more epistemic resources.

Unresolved: whether the intended target is the granularity/loss-of-discriminability objection, or the more metaphysical/external-world/other-minds or regress objection. The overwhelming weight of colleagues 1,2,3,4,6,8,9 converges on the heterogeneity / J+F vs UJ+T collapse.

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The question is about the coarse-graining forced by restricting the epistemic taxonomy to {Knowledge, Belief} under JTB = Justified True Belief.

Majority view from colleagues 1,2,3,4,6,8,9: Knowledge = B & J & T. With only two kinds, Belief is the complement of Knowledge, i.e. Belief = ¬(B&J&T). That makes Belief a heterogeneous grab-bag of the three non-knowledge cells in the Truth × Justification matrix.

The epistemic value of being responsibly held/evidence-responsive disappears outside knowledge.

* Unjustified True Belief, UJ+T. Not knowledge because not justified. On the two-state scheme it too must be called mere Belief. Hence a lucky true belief is epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief, and truth is lost as a discriminator once justification fails. The epistemic value of being true is invisible outside knowledge.

Thus Belief = J+F ∨ UJ+T ∨ UJ+F. Knowledge is homogeneous, Belief is disjunctive. The two non-Gettier collapses are therefore:
1. loss of discriminability for justification without truth – justified false belief cannot be marked off as better than unjustified false belief;
2. loss of discriminability for truth without justification – unjustified true belief cannot be marked off as different from false/unjustified belief.

I am keeping these as the core pre-Gettier over-lumping/lack-of-granularity problems.

Colleague 10 frames the problems as external-world skepticism and other-minds skepticism, i.e. whether justification can ever bridge to truth for those domains.

These are recorded as alternative readings but the weight of the round-0 discussion is on the heterogeneity/collapse of J+F and UJ+T into undifferentiated Belief.

Unresolved: whether the intended “two problems” are precisely the two collapse cases above, or the regress/circularity problem for J on a two-state ontology. Current best synthesis favors the collapse/granularity problems, with the regress point as a related meta-problem about how J can be non-circular without a third epistemic category.

That lumps a lucky true hit UJ+T together with justified false belief J+F and with unjustified false belief UJ+F. Truth is therefore invisible once justification fails; you cannot mark that a lucky true belief is epistemically defective relative to knowledge, and a true belief is conflated with false/unjustified belief.

Noted dissent / alternative framings:
- Colleague 10 proposes external world and other minds as the two problems; this is a scepticism problem rather than the granularity problem described above and is not supported by the rest.

If J = belief, justification collapses into more belief and yields infinite regress/circularity; if J = knowledge, knowledge is defined in terms of knowledge and the analysis becomes circular/redundant. My current leaning is the granularity / over-lumping reading: justified-false-belief problem and unjustified-true-belief/lucky-truth problem. Unresolved is whether the regress/circularity point is intended as a distinct second problem or as a formal consequence of the same granularity loss. Gettier is explicitly to be ignored.
reflection_text.6:
The question asks for the two non-Gettier problems JTB faces when the only epistemic kinds allowed are Knowledge and Belief.

Majority consensus in round 0: with JTB Knowledge = Belief ∧ Justified ∧ True, the complement Belief has to contain all non-knowledge cases. Truth and Justification are independent dimensions giving four cells:

J+T = Knowledge
J+F = justified false belief
UJ+T = unjustified true belief
UJ+F = unjustified false belief

With only Knowledge vs Belief the last three cells are forced into the single Belief state, making Belief a heterogeneous grab-bag and erasing independent epistemic value of justification and truth outside knowledge.

Problem 1, justification without truth: justified false belief J+F is not knowledge because false, so must be called mere Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from unjustified false belief UJ+F and from unjustified true belief UJ+T. Intuitively a justified error is epistemically better than an unjustified error, but the two-state taxonomy cannot register that; justification is invisible once truth fails.

Problem 2, truth without justification: unjustified true belief UJ+T is not knowledge because unjustified, so must be called mere Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from justified false belief J+F and from UJ+F. Intuitively a lucky true belief is epistemically defective compared with justified true belief, and also different from a false belief; truth is invisible once justification fails.

Hence Belief = J+F ∨ UJ+T ∨ UJ+F. Knowledge is homogeneous; Belief is disjunctive. The two-state scheme cannot mark a distinct state of justified non-knowledge or true non-knowledge.

Dissents to keep track of:
Colleague 10 frames the two problems as external world and other minds, i.e., whether justification/truth can ever be jointly satisfied for those domains without more epistemic resources.
Colleague 5 and 7 frame the problem as regress/circularity for the justification condition on an impoverished {B,K} ontology: J as belief collapses justification into belief and yields infinite regress, circularity, or dogmatism; J as knowledge makes JTB circular and requires higher-order knowledge ascent.

Unresolved: whether the intended target is the granularity/loss-of-discriminability objection, or the more metaphysical/external-world/other-minds or regress objection. The overwhelming weight of colleagues 1,2,3,4,6,8,9 converges on the heterogeneity / J+F vs UJ+T collapse.
reflection_text.8:
The question is about the cost of limiting the epistemic taxonomy to only Knowledge and Belief under JTB = Justified True Belief.

Consensus view from colleagues 1,2,3,4,6,8,9: With Truth x Justification you have 4 cells. JTB makes only J+T+B = Knowledge. Everything else is forced into the residual category Belief. That makes Belief a heterogeneous grab-bag.

The two non-Gettier collapses that are repeatedly identified are:

* Justification without truth is lost. Justified False Belief, J+F, is not Knowledge because it is not true. On a Know/Believe only scheme it must be called mere Belief. Hence a justified falsehood is epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified falsehood UJ+F. Justification has no visible epistemic value once truth fails; you cannot mark a responsible error as better than a careless error.

* Truth without justification is lost. Unjustified True Belief, UJ+T, is not Knowledge because it lacks justification. On a Know/Believe only scheme it must also be called mere Belief. Hence a lucky true belief is epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth has no visible epistemic value once justification fails; you cannot mark a lucky hit as different from a falsehood.

Thus Belief = J+F ∨ UJ+T ∨ UJ+F. Knowledge is homogeneous JTB; Belief is the disjunction of three distinct epistemic situations, so independent value of justification and of truth is erased outside knowledge.

Minority / divergent proposals noted:
Colleague 10 frames the two problems as external-world and other-minds skepticism, i.e. inability to bridge internal justification to external truth with only Know/Believe resources.
Colleague 5 and 7 frame the problem as internal to justification: if J must be cashed out in the impoverished ontology {B,K}, it is either belief → regress/circularity and justification can be by false belief, or knowledge → higher-order knowledge ascent / circular definition, and the justification clause becomes redundant.

I am currently tracking the majority heterogeneity/loss-of-granularity reading as the intended answer, with the justified-false-belief problem and the unjustified-true-belief/lucky-truth problem as the two specific collapses. The external world/other minds and regress/circularity readings remain noted as alternative interpretations from colleagues 10,5,7.
reflection_text.9:
The question is about the coarse-graining forced by restricting the epistemic taxonomy to {Knowledge, Belief} under JTB = Justified True Belief.

Majority view from colleagues 1,2,3,4,6,8,9: Knowledge = B & J & T. With only two kinds, Belief is the complement of Knowledge, i.e. Belief = ¬(B&J&T). That makes Belief a heterogeneous grab-bag of the three non-knowledge cells in the Truth × Justification matrix.

* Justified False Belief, J+F. Not knowledge because not true. On a Knowledge/Belief only scheme it must be called mere Belief. Hence a justified false belief is epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief UJ+F, and justification is lost as a discriminator once truth fails. The epistemic value of being responsibly held/evidence-responsive disappears outside knowledge.

* Unjustified True Belief, UJ+T. Not knowledge because not justified. On the two-state scheme it too must be called mere Belief. Hence a lucky true belief is epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief, and truth is lost as a discriminator once justification fails. The epistemic value of being true is invisible outside knowledge.

Thus Belief = J+F ∨ UJ+T ∨ UJ+F. Knowledge is homogeneous, Belief is disjunctive. The two non-Gettier collapses are therefore:
1. loss of discriminability for justification without truth – justified false belief cannot be marked off as better than unjustified false belief;
2. loss of discriminability for truth without justification – unjustified true belief cannot be marked off as different from false/unjustified belief.

I am keeping these as the core pre-Gettier over-lumping/lack-of-granularity problems.

Dissent / alternative framings noted:
Colleague 10 frames the problems as external-world skepticism and other-minds skepticism, i.e. whether justification can ever bridge to truth for those domains.
Colleague 5 and 7 frame the problem in terms of the justification condition itself on an impoverished ontology: if J must be cashed out in {B,K}, J identified with belief gives regress/circularity and the possibility of true belief being justified by false belief; J identified with knowledge gives higher-order knowledge ascent/circularity, making justification redundant.
These are recorded as alternative readings but the weight of the round-0 discussion is on the heterogeneity/collapse of J+F and UJ+T into undifferentiated Belief.

Unresolved: whether the intended “two problems” are precisely the two collapse cases above, or the regress/circularity problem for J on a two-state ontology. Current best synthesis favors the collapse/granularity problems, with the regress point as a related meta-problem about how J can be non-circular without a third epistemic category.

7.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 5's regress/circularity framing assumes we can still treat justification as an independent clause that then triggers foundationalist worries, but that already presupposes the very extra category (something between B and K) that the two-state restriction rules out from the start. Once we are limited to Knowledge vs. Belief, the only live question is what happens to the three non-K cells in the usual 2×2 matrix; they must all be absorbed into the single undifferentiated Belief bucket. That forces exactly the two collapses the rest of us have been describing: a justified false belief becomes indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief, and an unjustified true belief becomes indistinguishable from either of those or from a plain false belief. Both losses of discrimination are direct consequences of the binary taxonomy and do not require any further regress story. The heterogeneity objection therefore remains the more parsimonious account of the two non-Gettier problems under the stated constraint.

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: Colleague 5's regress worry is worth noting, but it seems to presuppose that we are already trying to analyze justification in terms of further beliefs or knowledge; that issue only surfaces once we have already lost the ability to mark justification and truth as independent dimensions. With only the two states Knowledge and Belief available, the 2x2 matrix of Truth × Justification is forced to collapse into a single undifferentiated Belief cell for every non-knowledge case. That immediately erases the distinction between a justified false belief (epistemically responsible error) and an unjustified false belief, and between an unjustified true belief (lucky hit) and a false belief. Those two losses of granularity—JFB and UTB—are the direct, pre-Gettier costs of the binary taxonomy, and they obtain even before any regress or circularity question arises about how to cash out J itself. The majority view among us therefore still seems right: the two problems are precisely the invisibility of justification once truth fails and the invisibility of truth once justification fails.

2.text:
With Knowledge = JTB and Belief = everything else the 2x2 of Truth × Justification is coarse grained to Knowledge vs non-Knowledge.

Knowledge = B ∧ J ∧ T

Belief on the binary taxonomy = ¬[B ∧ J ∧ T] = 
 J ∧ F ∧ B  ∨  UJ ∧ T ∧ B  ∨  UJ ∧ F ∧ B

Belief is therefore a heterogeneous grab-bag and the independent epistemic value of J and of T disappears as soon as you are out of Knowledge.

* Justification without truth is invisible. 
A justified false belief J+F is not knowledge because it is false, so on the {Know,Believe} taxonomy it must be called mere Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief UJ+F. A responsibly held, well-supported error is lumped with a careless error. Justification has no distinct non-knowledge status; its credit is erased once truth fails. That is the justified-false-belief problem.

* Truth without justification is invisible.
An unjustified true belief UJ+T is not knowledge because it is not justified, so on the two-state scheme it must also be called mere Belief. It is then epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false belief J+F and from an unjustified false belief UJ+F. A lucky true hit is lumped with a well-justified falsehood and with plain false belief. Truth has no distinct non-knowledge status; its credit is erased once justification fails. That is the unjustified-true-belief / lucky-truth problem.

Knowledge is homogeneous, Belief is disjunctive, and JTB on a Knowledge/Believe only ontology cannot register a distinct state of justified non-knowledge nor of true non-knowledge. With a binary taxonomy {Know, Believe} JTB can mark only the conjunction B & T & J.

Believe p = ¬Know p

* J + F = justified false belief
* UJ + T = unjustified true belief
* UJ + F = unjustified false belief

Belief therefore becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag and the independent epistemic value of T and J is invisible outside Knowledge.

Believe p = ¬Know p

So Belief is the disjunction of the three non-knowledge cells of the Truth × Justification matrix:

* J + F = justified false belief
* UJ + T = unjustified true belief
* UJ + F = unjustified false belief

Belief therefore becomes a heterogeneous grab-bag and the independent epistemic value of T and J is invisible outside Knowledge.

1. Justification without truth is invisible. A justified false belief is not Knowledge because it is false, so on a Know/Believe scheme it is mere Believe. It is thus epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified false belief, UJ+F, and indeed from an unjustified true belief. A responsibly held error, epistemically good in the justification respect, is lumped with a careless error. Justification ceases to be a discriminating norm once truth fails.

2. Truth without justification is invisible. An unjustified true belief is not Knowledge because it is unjustified, so on a Know/Believe scheme it is mere Believe. It is thus epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false belief J+F and from an unjustified false belief UJ+F. A lucky true hit is lumped with a well-justified falsehood and with outright false belief. Truth ceases to be a discriminating norm once justification fails.

Hence JTB with only Knowledge and Belief can mark Justified+True+Believe as Know but cannot mark a justified non-knowledge state distinct from an unjustified non-knowledge state, nor a true non-knowledge state distinct from a false non-knowledge state. That is the pre-Gettier over-lumping of Belief into J+F, UJ+T and UJ+F. The justification-without-truth and truth-without-justification collapses are the two non-Gettier granularity costs of the binary taxonomy.

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The consensus emerging here is exactly right and should be treated as settled: with only Knowledge and Belief available, JTB collapses the Truth × Justification matrix so that Belief must absorb J+F, UJ+T and UJ+F alike. That immediately erases two independent distinctions that JTB itself treats as normatively significant. Justification without truth becomes invisible because a responsibly held false belief is forced into the same undifferentiated Belief category as any unjustified falsehood; nothing in the taxonomy can register the epistemic credit that justification is supposed to confer when truth fails. Truth without justification likewise disappears because an unjustified true belief is lumped together with justified false beliefs and plain false beliefs, so the taxonomy cannot mark the epistemic defect that lack of justification introduces when truth happens to obtain. Both losses are forced directly by the binary constraint and by the JTB analysis itself; they are not downstream sceptical or meta-justificatory worries. Colleague 10’s point is therefore decisive: once the 2×2 is already collapsed into a single non-Knowledge cell, regress or circularity questions about how to cash out J become secondary and do not explain the primary granularity failure. External-world or other-minds concerns are likewise orthogonal, since they presuppose we can already distinguish the relevant non-knowledge states that the taxonomy erases. The two collapses—J without T and T without J—are therefore the direct, pre-Gettier problems JTB encounters under the stated epistemic-state restriction.

1.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE:

On a JTB analysis with the state space restricted to {Know, Believe}

Know p  iff  B p ∧ J p ∧ T p
Believe p = ¬Know p = ¬[B ∧ J ∧ T]

With B held fixed the Truth × Justification space is

J+T = Knowledge
J+F = justified false belief
UJ+T = unjustified true belief
UJ+F = unjustified false belief

With only two kinds the three non-knowledge cells are forced into the single residual Believe class

Believe = J+F ∨ UJ+T ∨ UJ+F

Knowledge is homogeneous JTB, Belief is a heterogeneous grab-bag. The binary taxonomy therefore erases the independent normative value of J and of T once you are out of Knowledge.

1. Justification without truth is erased, no distinct state for justified non-knowledge.
J+F is not Knowledge because it is false, so on a Know/Believe taxonomy it must be called mere Belief. Belief then has to contain both J+F and UJ+F, and also UJ+T. A responsibly held, evidence-responsive error is epistemically indistinguishable from a careless unjustified falsehood. Justification has no independent marking once truth fails; the epistemic credit of being justified is invisible outside Knowledge. That is the justified-false-belief / responsible-error problem.

2. Truth without justification is erased, no distinct state for true non-knowledge.
UJ+T is not Knowledge because it is not justified, so on a Know/Believe taxonomy it must also be called mere Belief. Belief then has to contain UJ+T together with J+F and UJ+F. A lucky true hit is epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth has no independent marking once justification fails; the epistemic value of being true is invisible outside Knowledge. That is the unjustified-true-belief / lucky-truth problem.

Hence JTB can only mark the conjunction J+T+B as Know. The independent value of justification for false beliefs and the independent value of truth for unjustified beliefs are swallowed by the undifferentiated Believe state. Belief = J+F ∪ UJ+T ∪ UJ+F; you cannot register a distinct state of justified non-knowledge nor of true non-knowledge. This is the pre-Gettier loss of granularity forced by the binary taxonomy.

3.text:
With only the two kinds Know and Believe, JTB can mark one cell of the Truth × Justification matrix and is forced to put the other three cells into the residual Believe class.

Know p iff B p & J p & T p
Believe p = ¬Know p = J∧F ∨ ¬J∧T ∨ ¬J∧F

Knowledge is homogeneous JTB, Belief is a heterogeneous grab-bag. The binary taxonomy erases the independent discriminability of J and T once you are out of Knowledge.

1. Justification without truth is invisible. J+F is not Knowledge because it is false, so on a Know/Believe taxonomy it must be called mere Belief. Belief therefore has to contain J+F together with UJ+F and UJ+T. A responsibly held, evidence-responsive error is epistemically indistinguishable from a careless, unjustified falsehood. Justification has no independent non-knowledge status; the epistemic credit of being justified is erased once truth fails. There is no distinct state for justified non-knowledge.

2. Truth without justification is invisible. UJ+T is not Knowledge because it is unjustified, so on a Know/Believe taxonomy it must also be called mere Belief. Belief therefore has to contain UJ+T together with J+F and UJ+F. A lucky true hit is epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth has no independent non-knowledge status; the epistemic value of being true is erased once justification fails. There is no distinct state for true non-knowledge.

Hence JTB on a Knowledge/Believe only ontology can mark only the conjunction J+T+B as Know. Both the independent value of justification for false beliefs and the independent value of truth for unjustified beliefs are swallowed by the undifferentiated Believe state. That is the pre-Gettier loss of granularity: no distinct marking for justified non-knowledge and no distinct marking for true non-knowledge.

4.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: With the state space restricted to {Know, Believe} and JTB = B ∧ J ∧ T

Know p iff B p ∧ J p ∧ T p
Believe p = ¬Know p

On the truth × justification matrix with belief held fixed

J ∧ T = Knowledge
J ∧ F = justified false belief
¬J ∧ T = unjustified true belief
¬J ∧ F = unjustified false belief

With only two kinds Believe is the complement of Know:

Believe = ¬[B ∧ J ∧ T] = J ∧ F ∨ ¬J ∧ T ∨ ¬J ∧ F

Knowledge is homogeneous, Believe is a heterogeneous grab-bag. The independent normative value of J and of T can only be registered together in Knowledge.

1. Justification without truth is invisible. J ∧ F is not Knowledge because it is false, so on a Know/Believe taxonomy it must be called mere Believe. A justified false belief is therefore epistemically indistinguishable from ¬J ∧ F and from ¬J ∧ T. A responsibly held, evidence-responsive error is lumped with a careless unjustified falsehood. Justification has no independent non-knowledge marking; the epistemic credit of being justified is erased once truth fails. No distinct state for justified non-knowledge exists.

2. Truth without justification is invisible. ¬J ∧ T is not Knowledge because it is unjustified, so on the two-state scheme it too must be called mere Believe. An unjustified true belief is therefore epistemically indistinguishable from J ∧ F and from ¬J ∧ F. A lucky true hit is lumped with a well-justified falsehood and with outright false belief. Truth has no independent non-knowledge marking; the epistemic value of being true is erased once justification fails. No distinct state for true non-knowledge exists.

Hence JTB on a binary taxonomy can mark only the conjunction J+T+B as Know. Both the independent value of justification for false beliefs and the independent value of truth for unjustified beliefs are swallowed by the undifferentiated Believe state. That is the pre-Gettier loss of granularity: no distinct state for justified non-knowledge and no distinct state for true non-knowledge.

Belief on a {Know, Believe} ontology = ¬[B ∧ J ∧ T] =

epistemically indistinguishable from J ∧ F and from ¬J ∧ F. A lucky true
hit is lumped with a well-justified falsehood and with plain false belief.
Truth has no independent non-knowledge home; its epistemic credit is erased
once justification fails. That is the unjustified-true-belief / lucky-truth
problem.

Hence with only Knowledge and Belief JTB can mark only the conjunction
J+T+B as Know. Both the independent value of justification for false

With JTB and Belief held fixed Knowledge occupies one cell of the Truth × Justification matrix

Know = B ∧ J ∧ T

and with only the two kinds Know/Believe the complement of Know is taken as Belief

Believe = ¬[B ∧ J ∧ T] = J ∧ F ∧ B  ∨  ¬J ∧ T ∧ B  ∨  ¬J ∧ F ∧ B

So Belief is forced to be the heterogeneous disjunction of the three non-knowledge cells. Knowledge is homogeneous, Belief does the work of three different epistemic situations and the independent normative value of J and of T is erased outside Knowledge.

Justification has no independent marking once truth fails; the epistemic credit of being justified is invisible outside Knowledge. There is no distinct state for justified non-knowledge.

2. Truth without justification is erased. 
¬J+T is not Knowledge because it is not justified, so on a Know/Believe taxonomy it too must be called mere Belief. An unjustified true belief is therefore epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false belief J+F and from an unjustified false belief ¬J+F. A lucky true hit is lumped with a well-justified falsehood and with outright false belief. Truth has no independent marking once justification fails; the epistemic value of being true is invisible outside Knowledge. There is no distinct state for true non-knowledge.

Hence JTB on a binary taxonomy can mark only J+T+B as Know. Both a distinct state of justified non-knowledge and a distinct state of true non-knowledge are lost; Belief = J+F ∪ UJ+T ∪ UJ+F. 6.text:
With only the two kinds {Know, Believe} the JTB analysis collapses the Truth × Justification matrix to a single positive cell.

Know p  iff B p ∧ J p ∧ T p
Believe p  := ¬Know p  = B p ∧ [ J p ∧ ¬T p  ∨  ¬J p ∧ T p  ∨  ¬J p ∧ ¬T p ]

So Believe is forced to be the heterogeneous disjunction

Believe = J+F  ∨  UJ+T  ∨  UJ+F

Knowledge is homogeneous, Believe is a grab-bag. That forces two independent pre-Gettier losses of discriminability.

1. Justification without truth is invisible. No home for a justified non-knowledge state.
J+F is not Knowledge because it is false, so on a Know/Believe taxonomy it must be called mere Belief. Believe then has to contain both J+F and UJ+F. A responsibly held, evidence-responsive error is epistemically indistinguishable from a careless unjustified falsehood. Justification has no independent marking once truth fails; the epistemic credit of being justified is invisible outside Knowledge. There is no distinct state for justified non-knowledge.

2. Truth without justification is invisible. No home for a true non-knowledge state.
UJ+T is not Knowledge because it is unjustified, so on a Know/Believe taxonomy it must also be called mere Belief. Believe then has to contain UJ+T together with J+F and UJ+F. A lucky true hit is epistemically indistinguishable from a justified false belief and from an unjustified false belief. Truth has no independent marking once justification fails; the epistemic value of being true is invisible outside Knowledge. There is no distinct state for true non-knowledge.

Hence on the binary taxonomy JTB can only mark the conjunction J+T+B as Know. Justification detached from truth and truth detached from justification are both swallowed by the undifferentiated Believe state. That is the classic pre-Gettier coarse-graining cost: the binary ontology cannot register a distinct justified false belief and cannot register a distinct unjustified true belief.

public_text.7: The consensus view among us is clearly the right one: under the binary {Knowledge, Belief} restriction, JTB forces Belief to absorb the three non-K cells of the Truth × Justification matrix, erasing independent normative marking for both J-without-T and T-without-J. This pre-Gettier granularity failure stands on its own even if one were to bracket later worries about how J itself might be analyzed; the two-state ontology already collapses the distinctions before any such meta-question arises. That keeps the account parsimonious and directly tied to the stated constraint.

Believe p = ¬Know p = ¬[B ∧ J ∧ T]

J+F = justified false belief
UJ+T = unjustified true belief
UJ+F = unjustified false belief

With only two kinds the three non-knowledge cells are forced into the single residual class

Believe = J+F ∨ UJ+T ∨ UJ+F

public_text.7: The emerging consensus is holding up well under scrutiny: once the ontology is restricted to {Know, Believe}, JTB’s Truth × Justification matrix is collapsed so that Belief must serve as the single undifferentiated residue for J+F, UJ+T and UJ+F. This is not merely a classificatory inconvenience; it erases the normative credit that JTB itself assigns to justification when truth fails and to truth when justification fails. A responsibly formed false belief thereby loses any distinguishable epistemic standing relative to an unjustified falsehood, and an unjustified true belief is rendered indistinguishable from either. Both distinctions are pre-Gettier and internal to the JTB analysis; they arise directly from the binary constraint rather than from later sceptical or meta-epistemic questions about how J is itself to be justified. Treating regress or circularity worries as primary would therefore mislocate the problem: those worries presuppose we can already mark the very non-knowledge states the taxonomy has already erased. The two granularity failures—absence of a distinct home for justified non-knowledge and absence of a distinct home for true non-knowledge—remain the direct, forced consequences of the stated restriction.
public_text.10: The emerging agreement across the group is well-supported and should be treated as the core diagnosis here. Under the strict {Know, Believe} restriction, JTB’s Truth × Justification matrix is forced into a single positive cell, so the three remaining cells collapse into an undifferentiated Believe category. This directly produces the two pre-Gettier losses of discriminability: justification detached from truth becomes invisible (a responsibly held false belief is lumped with unjustified falsehoods, erasing any independent epistemic credit for J when T fails), and truth detached from justification likewise disappears (an unjustified true belief is indistinguishable from both justified and unjustified false beliefs, erasing any independent value for T when J fails). These are not downstream meta-issues about how J is to be analyzed; they are immediate consequences of the binary taxonomy itself. Regress or circularity worries about justification are therefore secondary at best, since the taxonomy has already erased the very non-knowledge states those worries would need to distinguish. The two granularity failures—J without T and T without J—remain the direct problems JTB encounters once only Knowledge and Belief are available.

10.text: PUBLIC RESPONSE: The group’s converging diagnosis looks increasingly solid: under the strict {Know, Believe} restriction, JTB’s Truth × Justification matrix is reduced to a single admissible cell, forcing the three remaining cells into an undifferentiated Believe residue. That immediately erases any distinct marking for justified non-knowledge and for true non-knowledge, so a responsibly formed false belief becomes epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified falsehood, and an unjustified true belief becomes indistinguishable from either. These two granularity failures are direct, pre-Gettier consequences of the binary taxonomy itself. Any subsequent worries about how justification is to be grounded—whether they take the form of regress or circularity—presuppose that we can already discriminate the very non-knowledge states the taxonomy has already collapsed. Treating those meta-issues as primary would therefore invert the order of explanation; the taxonomy has already rendered the distinctions they require invisible. The two forced losses of discriminability remain the problems JTB encounters once only Knowledge and Belief are available.

public_text.10: The group’s converging diagnosis looks increasingly solid: under the strict {Know, Believe} restriction, JTB’s Truth × Justification matrix is reduced to a single admissible cell, forcing the three remaining cells into an undifferentiated Believe residue. That immediately erases any distinct marking for justified non-knowledge and for true non-knowledge, so a responsibly formed false belief becomes epistemically indistinguishable from an unjustified falsehood, and an unjustified true belief becomes indistinguishable from either. These two granularity failures are direct, pre-Gettier consequences of the binary taxonomy itself. Any subsequent worries about how justification is to be grounded—whether they take the form of regress or circularity—presuppose that we can already discriminate the very non-knowledge states the taxonomy has already collapsed. Treating those meta-issues as primary would therefore invert the order of explanation; the taxonomy has already rendered the distinctions they require invisible. The two forced losses of discriminability remain the problems JTB encounters once only Knowledge and Belief are available.
public_text.7: The consensus emerging here is robust: with the epistemic space limited to {Know, Believe}, JTB’s Truth × Justification matrix collapses so that only the single cell J+T+B registers as Knowledge while the remaining three cells are forced into an undifferentiated Believe residue. This produces exactly the two pre-Gettier granularity failures already identified. Justification detached from truth loses any independent epistemic standing; a responsibly formed false belief is rendered indistinguishable from unjustified falsehoods, rendering the normative credit of J invisible outside Knowledge. Truth detached from justification likewise loses any independent standing; an unjustified true belief becomes indistinguishable from both justified and unjustified false beliefs, erasing the epistemic value of T when J fails. These losses are immediate structural consequences of the binary taxonomy itself rather than later questions about how justification is to be grounded. Once the three non-knowledge cells are collapsed into a single heterogeneous grab-bag, no further resources remain within the {Know, Believe} ontology to mark either a distinct justified non-knowledge state or a distinct true non-knowledge state. The binary restriction therefore erases precisely the distinctions JTB would otherwise require us to recognize.
